subproblem.title: Deformation of an integer multiplicity current onto the n-skeleton (Simon 6.5.1, (1)–(25))
subproblem.statement: Assume, as hypotheses of the statement, (VO) the frozen type of Submission.dtc_vanish_off_support: for all P, n, U, S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω disjoint from spt S, S(ω) = 0; (MR) the frozen type of Submission.cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure: for U open and an IMRep R representing T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), M_W(T) = R.measure(W) for every open W; (REP) the frozen type of Submission.cmc_exists_massRepresentation: for U open and T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with M_W(T) < ∞ for open W ⊂⊂ U there are a Borel measure μ (μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0, finite on compact subsets of U) and ξ (μ-a.e. strongly measurable, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x, α) with M_W(T) = μ(W) for open W, T(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ, and, if also M_W(∂T) < ∞ for open W ⊂⊂ U, μ(E) = 0 whenever Hⁿ(E) = 0; (IMC) the frozen type of Submission.cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub: (a) locality of approximate tangent spaces for Borel M ⊆ M' ⊆ U with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ (K ⊆ U compact); (b) the restriction (M ∩ E, θ, ξ) of an IMRep to a Borel E is an IMRep representing some current; (c) A − B is integer multiplicity for integer multiplicity A, B (U open); (d) |R.orient(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for Hⁿ-a.e. x in the carrier; (SL) the frozen type of Submission.cmc_slice_mass_bounds: for T ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U) and ∂T represented by measures (μ, ξ), (μ', ξ') with |ξ|, |ξ'| ≤ 1 a.e. and f L-Lipschitz there are A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ, B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ' with ∂A_t(η) = B_t(η) when tsupport η misses {f = t}, M_W(∂A_t − B_t) ≤ L·liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹μ(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}) and ∫⁻_{(a,b)} M_W(∂A_t − B_t)dt ≤ L·μ(W ∩ {a < f < b}). (These are exactly the frozen Lean types of the parent node's resolved dependencies, written as antecedents so that the child does not need those declarations; the parent instantiates them.) For all P, m ∈ ℕ (n := m + 1) there is c ∈ ℝ≥0 with c ≥ 1 such that for every integer multiplicity T ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (domain univ) with compact support, M(T) < ∞ and M(∂T) < ∞ there are Q₀ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), R₁ ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^P) and S₁ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with: Q₀ and R₁ integer multiplicity; T − Q₀ − S₁ = ∂R₁; spt Q₀ ⊆ L_n := {x : there is a set s of coordinate indices with P ≤ n + |s| and x_i ∈ ℤ for i ∈ s} (the n-skeleton of the unit cubical grid); M(Q₀) ≤ cM(T), M(∂Q₀) ≤ cM(∂T), M(R₁) ≤ cM(T), M(S₁) ≤ cM(∂T); spt Q₀ ∪ spt R₁ ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt T) and spt ∂Q₀ ∪ spt S₁ ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt ∂T) (Metric.cthickening, the closed thickening {x : dist(x, A) ≤ √P}).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, proof of 5.1, displays (1)–(25) (chapter-06.txt lines 1405–1928), as written out in steps E1–E5 of the parent proof. Differences from the parent's text:
 - the good centre, the retraction, the push-forward/homotopy calculus and the summation of integer multiplicity pieces are the sibling theorems cmcdt_good_center (GC), cmcdt_skeleton_retraction (RET), cmcdt_lipschitz_pushforward_homotopy (PF) and cmcdt_im_series (IMS);
 - the parent's X_ν are decomposed into the dyadic shells already used in its E3, and each shell is deformed with its own Lipschitz extension of ψ;
 - integrality of Q₀ and R₁ is obtained by summing the integer multiplicity shell contributions with IMS (this is the closing step of the parent's B3, applied directly to ψ_#X_0 + Σ_i ψ_#Y_i = Q₀ as in the parent's E4).

Notation. n := m + 1. (VO), (MR), (REP), (IMC), (SL) are the five displayed hypotheses (frozen types of Submission.dtc_vanish_off_support, cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, cmc_exists_massRepresentation, cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub, cmc_slice_mass_bounds). All currents are on univ in ℝ^P. For currents A, B, “A + B” abbreviates A − (0 − B) (the contract's subtraction is pointwise, and currents are equal when their values agree, GeometricCurrentOn.ext). ‖ω‖ := sup_x|ω(x)|, and |X(ω)| ≤ M(X)‖ω‖ for every current X. NC_k := k-currents with compact support, finite mass and (k ≥ 1) finite boundary mass; NC_k is closed under differences. Support facts used below (all from the definitions and (VO)): spt(A − B) ⊆ spt A ∪ spt B; spt ∂A ⊆ spt A; spt 0 = ∅; a current that vanishes on every test form whose support is disjoint from a closed set E has support in E (every x ∉ E has a ball with compact closure disjoint from E). L_n := {x : ∃ s, P ≤ n + |s|, x_i ∈ ℤ (i ∈ s)} is closed (a finite union of the closed sets {x : x_i ∈ ℤ, i ∈ s}).

1. Trivial cases. If n ≥ P then L_n = ℝ^P (s = ∅). Take Q₀ := T, R₁ := 0, S₁ := 0 and c := 1: T − T − 0 = 0 = ∂0, T and 0 are integer multiplicity, the mass bounds are equalities or 0 ≤ ·, and spt T ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt T), spt ∂T ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt ∂T), spt 0 = ∅. From now on n < P, so RET and GC apply. Let c_R > 0 be RET's constant, C_G := (GC's constant) + 1 > 0, c₄ := 8(1 + √P c_R), and
 c := max(1, c₄ⁿ(1 + 2C_G), √P 2ⁿ c₄ⁿ(1 + 2C_G), √P (2c₄)^{n−1}(1 + 2C_G), c₄^{n−1}(1 + 2C_G)),
 which depends only on P and m. Let (push, homot) be the operators given by PF applied to (VO), (MR), (REP), (IMC). The zero current (in every degree) is integer multiplicity: the IMRep with empty carrier, multiplicity 0 and orientation 0 represents it (∅ is Borel and countably rectifiable, the remaining fields hold vacuously, and the representing integral over ∅ is 0). Let T be as in the statement. If M(T) = 0 then T = 0 (|T(ω)| ≤ M(T)‖ω‖), ∂T = 0, and Q₀ = R₁ = S₁ = 0 work. Assume M(T) > 0.

2. Measures (parent E0, E2). Let R_T = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep of T and μ_T := R_T.measure. By (MR), μ_T(W) = M_W(T) for open W, so μ_T(ℝ^P) = M(T) < ∞, and μ_T(ℝ^P ∖ spt T) = 0 by (VO). Further:
 - T(ω) = ∫ ξ(ω) dμ_T (definition of Represents and of the density measure);
 - ξ is μ_T-a.e. strongly measurable (μ_T ≪ Hⁿ⌞M);
 - |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| μ_T-a.e. by (IMC)(d);
 - μ_T is finite on compact sets.
 Since M(∂T) < ∞, (REP) (U = univ) gives μ_∂, ξ_∂ with μ_∂(W) = M_W(∂T) for open W, |ξ_∂| ≤ 1 and ∂T(η) = ∫ ξ_∂(η) dμ_∂; moreover μ_∂(ℝ^P) = M(∂T) and μ_∂(ℝ^P ∖ spt ∂T) = 0 by (VO).

3. Good centre (parent E1; GC). GC applied to the finite measures μ_T, μ_∂ gives a with |a_i − 1/2| < 1/4 such that, for d := dist(·, L*(a)), L*(a) the set of y with at least m + 2 coordinates in a_i + ℤ,
 (6) μ_T({d < r}) ≤ C_G r^{n+1} M(T), (7) μ_∂({d < r}) ≤ C_G r^{n+1} M(∂T) for r ∈ (0, 1/4].
 In particular μ_T({d = 0}) = μ_∂({d = 0}) = 0.

4. Retraction (RET). RET with this a gives ψ with: if d(x) > 0 then ψ(x) ∈ L_n and |ψ(x) − x| ≤ √P; and ψ is (c_R/r)-Lipschitz on {d ≥ r} for r ∈ (0, 1/4]. For r ∈ (0, 1/4] let φ_r be the componentwise McShane extension of ψ|{d ≥ r} (Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_real for each coordinate x ↦ ψ(x)_i, which is (c_R/r)-Lipschitz on {d ≥ r}). Then φ_r : ℝ^P → ℝ^P is (√P c_R/r)-Lipschitz and φ_r = ψ on {d ≥ r}. Put Λ(r) := max(1, √P c_R/r); id and φ_r are Λ(r)-Lipschitz, and Λ(r) ≤ c₄2^j whenever r ≥ 2^{−j−3}.

5. Slicing and good radii (parent E2; Simon (8)–(10)). Apply (SL) with U = univ, k = m, T, μ := μ_T, μ' := μ_∂, ξ, ξ' := ξ_∂, f := d, L := 1 (d is 1-Lipschitz; the measures are finite on compact sets, and the a.e. bounds and representations hold by 2). This gives currents A_t ∈ 𝒟_n, B_t ∈ 𝒟_{n−1} with A_t(ω) = ∫_{d<t} ξ(ω) dμ_T, B_t(η) = ∫_{d<t} ξ_∂(η) dμ_∂, ∂A_t(η) = B_t(η) when tsupport η ∩ {d = t} = ∅, and, for Z_t := ∂A_t − B_t, M(Z_t) ≤ liminf_{h↓0} h^{−1}μ_T({t − h < d < t}). If m ≥ 1, write m = k' + 1 and apply (SL) also to ∂T, which has degree k' + 1 (k := k' = m − 1, μ := μ_∂, ξ := ξ_∂, μ' := 0, ξ' := 0, valid because ∂∂T = 0; f := d). Its A'_t has the same values as B_t, so A'_t = B_t; its B'_t = 0; and M(∂B_t) ≤ liminf_{h↓0} h^{−1}μ_∂({t − h < d < t}).
 F(t) := μ_T({d < t}) and F_∂(t) := μ_∂({d < t}) are nondecreasing and finite, and μ_T({t − h < d < t}) ≤ F(t) − F(t − h), likewise for μ_∂. At every t where F and F_∂ are differentiable (all t outside a Lebesgue null set, Mathlib Monotone.ae_differentiableAt), M(Z_t) ≤ F'(t) and M(∂B_t) ≤ F_∂'(t) < ∞. For ν ≥ 0 let ρ_ν := 2^{−ν−2}. F' is measurable and ∫_{ρ_ν/2}^{ρ_ν} F' ≤ F(ρ_ν) − F(ρ_ν/2) ≤ μ_T({d < ρ_ν}) ≤ C_G ρ_ν^{n+1}M(T) (Mathlib MonotoneOn.intervalIntegrable_deriv, MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_deriv_mem_uIcc, and (6)). By Markov's inequality, F' > 4C_Gρ_νⁿM(T) on a subset of (ρ_ν/2, ρ_ν) of measure ≤ ρ_ν/4. As (ρ_ν/2, ρ_ν) has length ρ_ν/2 > ρ_ν/4, there is r_ν := ρ*_ν ∈ (ρ_ν/2, ρ_ν) at which F and F_∂ are differentiable and F'(r_ν) ≤ 4C_Gρ_νⁿM(T). Hence
 (10) M(Z_{r_ν}) ≤ 4C_Gρ_νⁿM(T) and M(∂B_{r_ν}) < ∞ (if m ≥ 1).
 (The parent also asks μ_T({d = r_ν}) = 0; this is not needed below because the shells are taken half-open.)
 Since r_{ν+1} < ρ_{ν+1} = ρ_ν/2 < r_ν, the r_ν strictly decrease to 0, r_ν ≤ 1/4 and r_ν > 2^{−ν−3}. Write A_ν := A_{r_ν}, B_ν := B_{r_ν}, Z_ν := Z_{r_ν}.

6. The pieces (parent E3). For j ≥ 0 define W_0 := T − A_0, W_j := A_{j−1} − A_j (j ≥ 1), D_0 := ∂T − B_0, D_j := B_{j−1} − B_j (j ≥ 1). Let E_0 := {d ≥ r_0} and E_j := {r_j ≤ d < r_{j−1}} (j ≥ 1).
 (6a) W_j(ω) = ∫_{E_j} ξ(ω) dμ_T and D_j(η) = ∫_{E_j} ξ_∂(η) dμ_∂. Hence M(W_0) ≤ M(T) and M(D_0) ≤ M(∂T), and for j ≥ 1, by (6), (7) with r_{j−1} < ρ_{j−1} = 2^{−j−1}: M(W_j) ≤ C_G 2^{−(j+1)(n+1)}M(T) and M(D_j) ≤ C_G 2^{−(j+1)(n+1)}M(∂T).
 (6b) W_j is integer multiplicity: (IMC)(b) with E := E_j gives a current represented by (M ∩ E_j, θ, ξ), whose values are ∫_{E_j} ξ(ω) dμ_T = W_j(ω).
 (6c) Supports: spt W_j ⊆ spt T ∩ closure(E_j) ⊆ spt T ∩ {d ≥ r_j} and spt D_j ⊆ spt ∂T ∩ {d ≥ r_j}. Indeed, if ω vanishes on spt T ∩ closure(E_j), the integrand of (6a) vanishes μ_T-a.e. on E_j (μ_T(ℝ^P ∖ spt T) = 0), so W_j vanishes on forms supported off this closed set. spt Z_j ⊆ {d = r_j} by the third clause of (SL). Also spt A_t ⊆ spt T and spt B_t ⊆ spt ∂T ⊆ spt T, so all supports above are compact.
 (6d) Boundaries: ∂A_t = B_t + Z_t, hence ∂W_0 = D_0 − Z_0 and ∂W_j = D_j + Z_{j−1} − Z_j (j ≥ 1). For m ≥ 1, ∂D_0 = −∂B_0, ∂D_j = ∂B_{j−1} − ∂B_j and ∂Z_j = −∂B_j have finite mass by (10). Hence W_j ∈ NC_n and D_j, Z_j ∈ NC_{n−1} (for m = 0 there is no boundary condition in degree 0).
 (6e) Σ_{j=0}^{N} W_j = T − A_N and M(A_N) ≤ μ_T({d < r_N}) ≤ C_G ρ_N^{n+1}M(T) → 0.

7. Deforming the pieces (parent E3, (11)–(20)). For j ≥ 0 let φ_j := φ_{r_j} and Λ_j := Λ(r_j) ≤ c₄2^j (as r_j > 2^{−j−3}); Λ_j ≤ Λ_{j+1}. Then φ_j = ψ on spt W_j ∪ spt D_j ∪ spt Z_j ⊆ {d ≥ r_j}, and φ_{j+1} = ψ = φ_j on spt Z_j ⊆ {d = r_j} ⊆ {d ≥ r_{j+1}}. Define
 V_j := push n φ_j W_j, H_j := homot n id φ_j W_j, Y_j := push (n−1) φ_j D_j, E'_j := homot (n−1) id φ_j D_j, L_j := push (n−1) φ_j Z_j, K_j := homot (n−1) id φ_j Z_j.
 - By PF (locality, maps Λ_{j+1}-Lipschitz): push (n−1) φ_{j+1} Z_j = L_j and homot (n−1) id φ_{j+1} Z_j = K_j.
 - By PF (identity and homotopy formula in degree n = m + 1, with F = id, G = φ_j, Λ = Λ_j): V_j − W_j − homot (n−1) id φ_j (∂W_j) = ∂H_j.
 - By PF (linearity, all pieces in NC_{n−1}) and (6d): homot (n−1) id φ_j (∂W_0) = E'_0 − K_0 and homot (n−1) id φ_j (∂W_j) = E'_j + K_{j−1} − K_j (j ≥ 1).
 - By PF (boundary commutation and linearity): ∂V_0 = Y_0 − L_0 and ∂V_j = Y_j + L_{j−1} − L_j (j ≥ 1).
 Summing over j = 0,…,N (telescoping):
 (S1) Σ_{j≤N}(V_j − W_j − ∂H_j) = Σ_{j≤N}E'_j − K_N, (S2) ∂(Σ_{j≤N}V_j) = Σ_{j≤N}Y_j − L_N.
 W_j is integer multiplicity, so by the integrality clause of PF (degree k + 1 = n), push n φ_j W_j = V_j is integer multiplicity (with F := φ_j) and homot n id φ_j W_j = H_j is integer multiplicity (with F := id, G := φ_j).
 Estimates (PF mass bounds; |φ_j(x) − x| = |ψ(x) − x| ≤ √P on the supports, since d > 0 there):
 M(V_0) ≤ c₄ⁿM(T), M(V_j) ≤ c₄ⁿ2^{jn}C_G2^{−(j+1)(n+1)}M(T) ≤ c₄ⁿC_G2^{−j}M(T);
 M(H_0) ≤ √P(2c₄)ⁿM(T), M(H_j) ≤ √P(2c₄)ⁿC_G2^{−j}M(T);
 M(Y_0) ≤ c₄^{n−1}M(∂T), M(Y_j) ≤ c₄^{n−1}C_G2^{−2j}M(∂T); M(E'_0) ≤ √P(2c₄)^{n−1}M(∂T), M(E'_j) ≤ √P(2c₄)^{n−1}C_G2^{−2j}M(∂T);
 M(L_N) ≤ Λ_{N}^{n−1}M(Z_N) ≤ c₄^{n−1}2^{N(n−1)}·4C_G2^{−(N+2)n}M(T) ≤ 4C_Gc₄^{n−1}2^{−N}M(T) → 0, and likewise M(K_N) ≤ √P(2Λ_N)^{n−1}M(Z_N) → 0.
 Hence Σ_j M(V_j) ≤ c₄ⁿ(1 + 2C_G)M(T), Σ_j M(H_j) ≤ √P(2c₄)ⁿ(1 + 2C_G)M(T), Σ_j M(E'_j) ≤ √P(2c₄)^{n−1}(1 + 2C_G)M(∂T) and Σ_j M(Y_j) ≤ c₄^{n−1}(1 + 2C_G)M(∂T).

8. Limits (parent E4; IMS).
 - IMS (degree n = m + 1) gives Q₀ with Q₀(ω) = Σ_j V_j(ω): integer multiplicity, M(Q₀) ≤ Σ_j M(V_j) ≤ cM(T), spt Q₀ ⊆ closure ⋃_j spt V_j.
 - By (IMC)(c), 0 − H_j is integer multiplicity (0 and H_j are), with M(0 − H_j) ≤ M(H_j). IMS (degree m + 2) gives R₁ with R₁(ζ) = Σ_j(0 − H_j)(ζ): integer multiplicity, M(R₁) ≤ cM(T), spt R₁ ⊆ closure ⋃_j spt H_j.
 - IMS (degree m + 1, existence part) gives S₁ with S₁(ω) = Σ_j(0 − E'_j)(ω), M(S₁) ≤ cM(∂T), spt S₁ ⊆ closure ⋃_j spt E'_j.
 Identity (21). Evaluate (S1) at ω: Σ_{j≤N}V_j(ω) − T(ω) + A_N(ω) − Σ_{j≤N}H_j(dω) = Σ_{j≤N}E'_j(ω) − K_N(ω). As N → ∞, A_N(ω) → 0 and K_N(ω) → 0 (masses → 0), so Q₀(ω) − T(ω) + R₁(dω) = −S₁(ω), i.e. (T − Q₀ − S₁)(ω) = ∂R₁(ω). Hence T − Q₀ − S₁ = R₁.boundary.
 Boundary mass (25). The finite sums Ŝ_N := Σ_{j≤N}V_j converge weakly to Q₀, so ∂Ŝ_N converge weakly to ∂Q₀ (SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.boundary), and M(∂Q₀) ≤ liminf_N M(∂Ŝ_N) (SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf). By (S2), M(∂Ŝ_N) ≤ Σ_jM(Y_j) + M(L_N), so M(∂Q₀) ≤ c₄^{n−1}(1 + 2C_G)M(∂T) ≤ cM(∂T).

9. Supports (parent E5, (22)–(23)).
 - spt V_j ⊆ φ_j(spt W_j) = ψ(spt W_j) ⊆ L_n ∩ cthickening(√P, spt T) (RET, as d > 0 and the points lie in spt T). Both sets are closed, so spt Q₀ ⊆ L_n ∩ cthickening(√P, spt T).
 - spt H_j ⊆ {x + t(φ_j(x) − x) : x ∈ spt W_j, t ∈ [0,1]} ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt T) (PF), so spt R₁ ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt T) (spt(0 − H_j) ⊆ spt H_j).
 - Likewise spt E'_j ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt ∂T), so spt S₁ ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt ∂T).
 - Finally, if tsupport ω ∩ cthickening(√P, spt ∂T) = ∅, then Y_j(ω) = 0 for all j (spt Y_j ⊆ φ_j(spt D_j) ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt ∂T); (VO)). So ∂Ŝ_N(ω) = −L_N(ω) → 0 and ∂Q₀(ω) = lim ∂Ŝ_N(ω) = 0; hence spt ∂Q₀ ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt ∂T).

10. Q₀, R₁, S₁ satisfy all conclusions with the constant c of 1 (c ≥ 1): integrality (8), the identity (8), spt Q₀ ⊆ L_n (9), the four mass bounds (7)–(8) and the support inclusions (9). ∎
proof_key_steps: Trivial cases n ≥ P (Q₀ := T) and T = 0; constants from RET and GC.
Measures μ_T (IMRep, MR, VO) and μ_∂ (REP); good centre a with μ_T, μ_∂({d < r}) ≤ C r^{n+1}·mass (GC).
Retraction ψ (RET) and its McShane extensions φ_r with Lipschitz constant √P c_R/r.
Slicing (SL) and Lebesgue differentiation of F(t) = μ_T({d < t}) give radii r_ν ∈ (ρ_ν/2, ρ_ν) with M(Z_{r_ν}) ≤ 4Cρ_νⁿM(T) and finite boundary slices.
Dyadic shells W_j, D_j (integer multiplicity, normal, supports in {d ≥ r_j}) with ∂W_j = D_j + Z_{j−1} − Z_j.
PF: deformations V_j, homotopies H_j, E'_j; telescoping of the slice terms by locality; geometric mass estimates.
IMS: Q₀ := ΣV_j and R₁ := Σ(0 − H_j) integer multiplicity, S₁ := Σ(0 − E'_j); identity T − Q₀ − S₁ = ∂R₁; M(∂Q₀) by lower semicontinuity.
Supports: ψ maps into L_n and moves points by ≤ √P; homotopy supports; ∂Q₀ via vanishing of the deformed ∂T-pieces and of the slice terms in the limit.

audit.reason: The declared dependencies suffice. Good slicing radii make the shell and slice currents normal; locality cancels successive slice terms. Summable mass estimates and im_series yield the identity and integrality, while weak boundary convergence gives the boundary mass and support bounds. Constants are uniform in T, and n ≥ P and zero-current cases are covered.
